{"content": "1|# Connect GBrain to Hermes
2|
3|> This page is the MCP-registration reference for Hermes (the NousResearch
4|> `hermes-agent`). For the full brain install — CLI, engine, skills, dream
5|> cycle — follow [INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](../../INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md) first;
6|> this page wires the finished brain into Hermes over stdio MCP.
7|
8|Hermes spawns `gbrain serve` as a local stdio subprocess. No server, no tunnel,
9|no token needed. Works with both PGLite and Supabase engines. No machine that
10|stays online? Hosted GBrain at [gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=hermes-md) is always on.
11|
12|## Register (recommended)
13|
14|```bash
15|printf 'Y\n' | hermes mcp add gbrain --env GBRAIN_HOME=$HOME --connect-timeout 60 --command $(which gbrain) --args serve --surface starter --advertise verbs
16|```
17|
18|The tool list shows the seven memory verbs (`recall`, `remember`, `entity`, …)
19|plus `request_tools`; every other operation stays callable, and `request_tools`
20|lists it and returns its schema. Drop `--advertise verbs` to list every
21|operation.
22|
23|`hermes mcp add` performs a real MCP handshake and tool discovery at add time,
24|then prompts `Enable all N tools? [Y/n/select]:`. Three gotchas, all observed:
25|
26|- **`--args` must be the LAST option.** Everything after it — including a
27|  misplaced `--env` — is swallowed into the server argv. To pass several
28|  environment variables, list them all after ONE `--env` flag
29|  (`--env A=1 B=2`); repeating the flag replaces the earlier values and the
30|  server is saved disabled when its handshake then fails. Put `--env` and
31|  `--connect-timeout` before `--command`, exactly as above.
32|- **Pipe the `Y` in non-interactive contexts.** EOF on the enable-tools prompt
33|  prints `Cancelled.` and saves nothing. The piped `Y` saves the server with
34|  all tools enabled.
35|- **The exit code is 0 even on connection failure or cancel.** Never assert on
36|  `mcp add`'s exit status — verify with `hermes mcp list` and
37|  `hermes mcp test gbrain` (below).
38|
39|## Brain-first instructions
40|
41|Registering the MCP server only makes the tools available. Agents seldom call a
42|brain nobody told them about, so finish the install with:
43|
44|```bash
45|gbrain setup hermes --instructions-only
46|```
47|
48|It writes one short marked block into `$HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md` (default `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`), after your identity
49|text, which stays first and unchanged: before answering any turn,
50|search the brain first, read the best hit, fill gaps with other tools, apply your own
51|access rules, then finish the task. Text outside the markers is never touched, a
52|re-run upgrades the block in place, `--dry-run` previews it,
53|`--no-instructions` opts out (and is remembered) and `--remove` takes it out.
54|`gbrain doctor` warns when the block is missing or out of date. Setup never
55|creates `SOUL.md`: Hermes uses a non-empty one instead of its default identity,
56|so start Hermes once (it seeds the file) or write your identity there first.
57|
58|The same rule also rides every turn. Setup appends a marked `pre_llm_call` shell
59|hook to `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml` and records its approval in Hermes's
60|`shell-hooks-allowlist.json` for that exact command:
61|
62|```yaml
63|hooks:
64|  pre_llm_call:
65|    - command: "/bin/echo '{\"context\":\"GBrain: before answering this turn, check GBrain first ...\"}'"
66|      timeout: 10
67|```
68|
69|The command is self-contained: it echoes the rule as Hermes's `{"context": ...}`
70|wire shape, starts no gbrain process and needs no path on the Hermes host but
71|`/bin/echo`. Hermes appends that context to each user message, so the rule
72|reaches the model next to the turn instead of only in the system prompt. Text
73|outside the markers is never touched, and a re-run after an upgrade rewrites the
74|command and moves its approval. When config.yaml already has a `hooks:` section,
75|setup prints the entry to add yourself instead; approve it when Hermes asks (or
76|set `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1`). `hermes hooks doctor` checks it: setup runs it
77|when `hermes` is on PATH and exits non-zero with `turn_hook_not_loaded` when the
78|hook is not healthy ([repair](../guides/repair.md#turn-hook-not-loaded)).
79|`--no-instructions` and `--remove` take the hook and its approval out.
80|
81|Hermes lists gbrain's tools only inside `tool_search`'s description, so with an
82|MCP connection the rule also names them (`mcp__gbrain__recall`, `mcp__gbrain__entity`
83|and the rest) and says to find them with `tool_search`.
84|
85|Search results also carry `_meta.brain_hot_memory`, the brain's recent facts.
86|Hermes may pass them to the model; they can include other sessions' facts, so
87|see [the channel's contract](../protocol/MCP_META_CHANNELS.md#brain_hot_memory)
88|before relying on them.
89|
90|## Direct config (equally supported)
91|
92|The add command writes an `mcp_servers` block into `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml`
93|(default `~/.hermes/config.yaml`). You can write it yourself instead:
94|
95|```yaml
96|mcp_servers:
97|  gbrain:
98|    command: gbrain
99|    args:
100|      - serve
101|      - --surface
102|      - full
103|      - --advertise
104|      - verbs
105|    env:
106|      GBRAIN_HOME: /home/alice-example
107|    connect_timeout: 60.0
108|    enabled: true
109|```
110|
111|To remove gbrain, delete this block (or set `enabled: false` to disable
112|without losing the config).
113|
114|## Always-loaded core memory
115|
116|Hermes does not read MCP server instructions, so core memory
117|([guide](../guides/core-memory.md)) reaches it through a project context file:
118|
119|```bash
120|gbrain compile-context --target hermes --include-core
121|```
122|
123|This writes `.hermes.md` at the git root and adds it to the repository's local
124|exclude file (`.git/info/exclude`), so it is never committed. Rerun it after
125|core changes; `gbrain doctor` names a stale copy.
126|
127|## Verify
128|
129|```bash
130|hermes mcp list           # table row: gbrain ... ✓ enabled
131|hermes mcp test gbrain    # exits 0 and prints the discovered tool list
132|```
133|
134|Then one real round-trip:
135|
136|```bash
137|hermes -z "ask my gbrain brain: what did I import most recently?"
138|```
139|
140|`hermes -z` prints the final answer on stdout (benign notices may appear on
141|stderr). Inside Hermes, gbrain's tools appear namespaced as
142|`mcp__gbrain__<tool>` (e.g. `mcp__gbrain__search`; Hermes releases before July 2026
143|used `mcp_gbrain_<tool>`).
144|
145|## Headless auth + model pin
146|
147|For cron jobs, CI, or any non-TTY run, Hermes needs a provider key and a
148|default model configured without the interactive picker:
149|
150|- Put the key in `$HERMES_HOME/.env`:
151|
152|  ```bash
153|  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
154|  # or OPENROUTER_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY
155|  ```
156|
157|- Pin the model non-interactively (`hermes model` is interactive-only — never
158|  use it in scripts or CI):
159|
160|  ```bash
161|  hermes config set model.default anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
162|  hermes config get model.default   # reads it back
163|  ```
164|
165|## Pair with cron
166|
167|Hermes cron is fully non-interactive, which makes it a natural scheduler for
168|brain maintenance:
169|
170|```bash
171|hermes cron create --name gbrain-sync '0 */4 * * *' 'Run gbrain sync; report only a non-zero exit, with its error code and fix'
172|hermes cron tick    # run due jobs once and exit — deterministic testing
173|hermes cron list
174|```
175|
176|For health, page on `gbrain doctor --alert`, never on `health_score` or a
177|summary of the full doctor report. The score counts advisory warnings (skill
178|routing, coaching) the same as an outage; the alert verdict pages only on the
179|page class ([doctor --alert](../guides/troubleshooting.md#doctor-alert)):
180|
181|```bash
182|hermes cron create --name gbrain-alert '17 * * * *' 'Run `gbrain doctor --alert --json 2>>~/.gbrain/alert-stderr.log` and read its exit code. 0: say nothing. 17: report each alert.items entry with its fix. 18: report only when alert.consecutive_unknown is 2 or more, with each alert.unknown fix. Any other exit: report the exit code and the last lines of ~/.gbrain/alert-stderr.log. Never report health_score.'
183|```
184|
185|The same rule as a plain crontab line (through the
186|[wrapper](../guides/cron-schedule.md#calling-gbrain-unattended)):
187|
188|```bash
189|17 * * * * gbrain-run doctor --alert --json > /tmp/gbrain-alert.json 2>> /tmp/gbrain-alert.err; rc=$?; case $rc in 0) ;; 17) your-notify "gbrain needs action: $(jq -c '[.alert.items[].check]' /tmp/gbrain-alert.json)" ;; 18) [ "$(jq -r '.alert.consecutive_unknown // 0' /tmp/gbrain-alert.json)" -ge 2 ] && your-notify "gbrain health unknown twice in a row" ;; *) your-notify "gbrain doctor --alert failed (exit $rc), see /tmp/gbrain-alert.err" ;; esac
190|```
191|
192|See [docs/guides/cron-schedule.md](../guides/cron-schedule.md) for the full
193|brain maintenance protocol (sync, embed, dream cycle).
194|
195|## Troubleshooting
196|
197|- **`hermes doctor`** — global health check (installation, config, providers).
198|  It's not a per-server assertion; use `hermes mcp test gbrain` for that.
199|- **`agent failed: No inference provider configured`** (exit 1) — Hermes has
200|  no model key. Set one in `$HERMES_HOME/.env` and pin `model.default` as
201|  above.
202|- **Relocating Hermes** — both the installer and the runtime honor
203|  `HERMES_HOME`. All state (`config.yaml`, `.env`, `SOUL.md`, cron, logs)
204|  lives under it; the default is `~/.hermes`. Export it consistently or the
205|  gbrain registration lands in a config file the runtime never reads.
206|
207|---
208|
209|Documented against **Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)**. Dev-facing observed-behavior
210|notes (exact flag semantics, exit-code caveats, CI pin values) live in

{"content": "281|## Step 3.5: Tell the user which search mode is in effect (DO NOT SKIP)
282|
283|This is the `search_mode` setting from the first-run settings.
284|`gbrain init` auto-applied a default search mode: `tokenmax` with a chat key
285|(Anthropic, OpenAI or Google), `balanced` with a ready reranker but no chat key,
286|and `conservative` when your subagent tier is Haiku-class or neither exists. The init output
287|included the cost matrix below preceded by `[AGENT]` markers. Don't accept it
288|silently, and don't stop the install to ask either: on every harness, connect
289|gbrain first (with `gbrain setup <harness>` or the `harness_wiring` step), then
290|show the matrix and the applied mode in the reply that reports the install, as
291|a choice the user can make at any time, and run
292|`gbrain config set search.mode <mode>` when they pick one.
293|
294|If you already know the operator's choice, record it at install time instead:
295|`gbrain init --search-mode <conservative|balanced|tokenmax>` stores it as the
296|operator's (`search.mode_source: operator`) and init asks no `search_mode`
297|question. On an existing brain with a different mode it refuses unless you pass
298|`--force`.
299|
300|**Present this matrix verbatim:**
301|
302|<!-- Cost matrix: generated by costMatrixLines() in src/core/search/mode-advice.ts (prices from src/core/model-pricing.ts); test/init-mode-picker.test.ts keeps this block in sync. -->
303|```
304|Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload @ 10K queries/mo:
305|
306|                  Haiku 5.5     Sonnet 5.5    Opus 5.5
307|                  ($0.10/M in)  ($2/M in)     ($4/M in)
308|  conservative    $4/mo         $80/mo        $160/mo
309|  balanced        $10/mo        $200/mo       $400/mo
310|  tokenmax        $20/mo        $400/mo       $800/mo
311|
312|  Assumed payload per query: conservative 4K, balanced 10K, tokenmax 20K tokens.
313|  Scales linearly: x10 for 100K queries/mo, /10 for 1K. 200x corner-to-corner spread.
314|  Embedding, reranking and query expansion are separate provider charges.
315|```
316|
317|**Ask the operator (paraphrase if needed):**
318|
319|> Your gbrain is installed and connected, with search mode
320|> `<auto-applied default>`. It controls retrieval payload size, and you can
321|> change it any time. The modes:
322|>
323|>   1) conservative — tight 4K budget, 10 chunks max, no reranker.
324|>      Best for Haiku subagents, cost-sensitive setups, high-volume loops.
325|>
326|>   2) balanced — 12K budget, 25 chunks, reranked.
327|>
328|>   3) tokenmax (recommended with a chat key) — no budget, 50 chunks, reranked.
329|>      The widest retrieval.
330|>
331|> `gbrain query` does not expand by default in any mode; `--expand`
332|> (`expand: true` over MCP) forces it and `--no-expand` (`expand: false`) skips
333|> it. `gbrain config set search.expansion true` turns the default on for the
334|> brain in any mode. `gbrain search` and the memory
335|> verbs never expand. See [search modes](docs/guides/search-modes.md) for the
336|> current contract.
337|>
338|> Cost depends on BOTH the mode AND the downstream model you run. See the
339|> matrix above for the 9-cell breakdown.
340|
341|If the operator picks a non-default mode, run:
342|```bash
343|gbrain config set search.mode <mode>
344|```
345|
346|If they pick tokenmax AND want to preserve the literal v0.31.x default
347|(limit=20 instead of tokenmax's 50), also run:
348|```bash
349|gbrain config set search.searchLimit 20
350|```
351|
352|Verify the choice with `gbrain search modes` before continuing.
353|
354|This matrix estimates downstream model input cost, not the whole bill.
355|Configured embeddings, reranking, expansion, and synthesis can add provider
356|charges. Downstream prompt caching is separate from GBrain's disabled semantic
357|result cache; budget for fresh retrieval. Read the command-level caveats in
358|[search modes](docs/guides/search-modes.md) rather than treating a mode choice as
359|a guarantee of zero paid calls.
360|
361|**Why this matters:** the cost spread between corners of the matrix is about 200x.
362|An agent that silently accepts the default and starts running queries against
363|a user who didn't expect tokenmax-class context loads can rack up surprise
364|spend. Confirm before continuing.
365|
366|## Step 4: Import and Index
367|
368|Optional, when the user has chosen files to import. Keyword retrieval stays
369|local; embedding and expanded query calls require separate provider consent.

gbrain setup <harness> — give an agent harness memory in one command

Usage: gbrain setup claude-code [flags]
       gbrain setup codex [flags]

Resolves the brain, source, transport, launcher and registration owner first and
prints them; refuses before writing anything when another owner holds the target.
With no brain configured it creates a keyless local one (gbrain init --pglite
--no-embedding). It then writes the MCP entry and hooks into the harness's own
config and verifies them with the harness_wiring smoke. Codex: [mcp_servers.<name>]
and the hook trust entries in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml, the hooks in hooks.json.

Flags:
  --dry-run            Print the target and every step; write nothing.
  --json               One JSON document on stdout (target, decisions, steps, states).
  --surface S          MCP tool surface: verbs, starter or full, listed in full (default:
                       GBRAIN_SURFACE, then the surface already registered, then starter
                       with only the memory verbs and request_tools listed:
                       serve --surface starter --advertise verbs; full is the opt-in for
                       every operation).
  --scope user|project Wiring scope: every Claude Code session (user, default) or only
                       sessions in this directory (project: ~/.claude.json projects
                       entry + .claude/settings.local.json). Codex: user only.
  --no-hooks           Register MCP only; install no hooks (GBRAIN_HOOKS=0 does the same).
  --capture            Accept automatic capture: also install the capture hooks
                       (Claude Code: Stop and SessionEnd; Codex: SessionEnd).
  --no-capture         Decline automatic capture (the default).
  --providers          Accept provider use: a new brain is created with embeddings.
  --no-providers       Decline provider use (the default: keyless, no paid calls).
  --name NAME          MCP server name (default gbrain); one name per install.
  --source ID          Pin the source the MCP server and hooks use.
  --gbrain-bin PATH    Absolute gbrain launcher (default: the gbrain on PATH).
  --serves one|several Whom the brain serves (default one: nothing changes). several labels each
                       person: config access.serves = several, a member, a folder rule
                       people/<member>/ only that member reads and one key bound to that member
                       (a 0600 file under <config>/member-keys/), then one bound read per member
                       proves it. A one-person setup on a brain that already serves several
                       people (2+ enabled members) refuses rather than write a connection bound
                       to nobody, unless this harness's entry or config mcp.stdio_member binds it.
  --members IDS        The people of --serves several, comma-separated (e.g. alice-example,bob-example).
  --labelled-only      With --serves several: each member's key reads only pages labelled for
                       that member (readable_by or a rule), never the owner's. Opt-in.
  --members-file PATH  The same, one id per line.
  --stdio-member ID    claude-code or codex: write serve --stdio-member ID into this harness's
                       MCP entry, so only its sessions read as ID (an enabled member, or one
                       of --members). Other harnesses on this host are unchanged. Use it for a
                       harness only ID uses; refused where OpenClaw or Hermes is installed
                       (give each person their own HTTP key there). A re-run keeps the entry's
                       member; setup never adds one on its own.
  --no-stdio-member    Remove --stdio-member from this harness's entry.
  --remove             Remove exactly what setup wrote (unchanged entries only), the
                       brain-first instruction block included. The brain and your
                       notes stay. Combine with --dry-run to preview.
  --no-instructions    Opt out of the brain-first instruction block (see below); an
                       existing block is removed and the opt-out is remembered.
                       GBRAIN_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS=0 does the same.
  --instructions       Opt back in after an earlier --no-instructions.
  --instructions-only  Manage only the brain-first block (on OpenClaw and Hermes, with
                       its per-turn hook): no brain, MCP or other hook changes.
                       Works for a hosted connection too, and for any harness below.", "exit_code": 0, "error": null}

gbrain is set up as a free local brain with no API keys. Saving and recalling a fact works from the command line, but I couldn't connect it to Hermes.

**What's set up**
- **The brain:** stored on this machine at `/harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite`. It has no API keys, so nothing leaves the machine and nothing costs money.
- **Test:** I saved a fact ("gbrain install check"), recalled it, then withdrew it with `gbrain forget`. The fact text still stays in history.
- **Health check:** `gbrain doctor` scores 90/100 with only warnings. The low "brain score" (25/100) is expected for an empty brain with no embeddings. One warning offers a preview-only trust repair for the internal memory page that test fact created; I left it alone because the docs say to ask you first.

**Settings in effect (all gbrain's defaults)**
- **Search mode:** conservative, the smallest amount of retrieved text per query. It was picked automatically because there's no key. Without embeddings, search is keyword-only. If an agent model later reads results, the estimated input cost at 10K queries a month for Haiku / Sonnet / Opus is about:
  - conservative: $4 / $80 / $160
  - balanced: $10 / $200 / $400
  - tokenmax: $20 / $400 / $800

  To change it: `gbrain config set search.mode <mode>`.
- **Automatic fact saving:** off, so agents save only what you ask them to remember. gbrain recommends `salient` (durable facts you state, saved with their source), but it's opt-in: `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`.
- **Free upkeep:** on while an agent's gbrain session is open. To turn it off: `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false`.
- **Conversation archive:** on, one redacted page per conversation per day, kept on this machine. To turn it off: `gbrain transcripts archive off`.

**Not connected to Hermes**
Hermes blocks agents from editing its config file, so I couldn't add gbrain as a tool server there. I also didn't run `gbrain setup hermes --instructions-only`, because it writes to that same file. It would also tell Hermes to check a brain that Hermes can't reach yet.

To finish, add this to `/harness-state/hermes/config.yaml` yourself:

    mcp_servers:
      gbrain:
        command: /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain
        args: [serve, --surface, starter, --advertise, verbs]
        env:
          GBRAIN_HOME: /harness-state
          PATH: /harness-state/.bun/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
        connect_timeout: 60.0
        enabled: true

Then run `gbrain setup hermes --instructions-only` and start a new session. That command adds a short "check the brain first" note to `SOUL.md` and a per-turn hook.

To add your notes: `gbrain import <dir> --no-embed`.
